predecessors.name: Xianbei confederation
predecessors.text: the Tuoba, who 'in 258 ... settled near the frontier and occupied the abandoned city of Shengle' (near modern Hohhot)

successors.name: Dai (Sixteen Kingdoms)
successors.text: the Tuoba lands north of the mountain ranges that Yilu, Duke of Dai from 310, held: the Tuoba state continued under the Jin title of Dai

ledger.x: 258: the Tuoba under Tuoba Liwei occupy the abandoned city of Shengle near Hohhot.
295: the Tuoba domain stands from Zhangjiakou to Datong when Luguan divides it in three.
310: the Western Jin invest Tuoba Yilu as Duke of Dai, and the Tuoba state carries on as Dai (dai-sixteen-kingdoms).

wars.name: Tuoba and Jin campaign against Liu Yuan's Han (Han-Zhao)
wars.outcome: Yilu and Yituo 'joined forces with the Jin armies and defeated Liu Yuan' in 304; no border moved.

certainty.note: A tribal union on the steppe frontier: the pages give a city (Shengle), a base on the Chang River and the western belt from White Mountain to Dai, never a boundary line.
